questions.q: The printed hierarchy between the two radiosensitizers is:
questions.exp: 'Cisplatin > 5FU' on page 247.

questions.q: Vaginal fibrosis from chemoradiation causes which printed problem?
questions.exp: 'Vaginal fibrosis (Difficult intercourse)'.

questions.q: Ovarian failure after radiation is explained on the page because:
opts: Ovary is the most radiosensitive organ
Ovaries lie in the radiation field always
questions.exp: 'Ovarian failure : Ovary is most radiosensitive organ'.

questions.q: The two side effects bracketed together explain why:
opts: Surgery is not preferred in early stages
RT is not preferred in late stages
RT is not preferred in early stages
questions.exp: The bracket label reads 'RT not preferred in early stages'.

questions.q: Match each chemoradiation attribute with its printed value - 1) Indication stages 2) Best radiosensitizer 3) Timing 4) Key side effect ... A) Cisplatin B) Prior to RT C) IB3, IIA2 to IV D) Ovarian failure ... choose:
questions.exp: Indication is IB3 to IV, cisplatin leads, given before RT, with ovarian failure as the highlighted side effect.

questions.q: Scenario: A 34-year-old with stage IIA2 cancer cervix is planned for organ-preserving non-surgical therapy. The printed regimen category is:
questions.exp: IIA2 sits inside the printed chemoradiation indication range.

questions.q: Brachytherapy's source of radiation is printed as:
questions.exp: The table prints 'Inside body' for brachytherapy source.

questions.q: Brachytherapy is also described as which therapy type?
questions.exp: 'Intracavitary therapy' is the second brachy bullet.

questions.q: The applicators printed for brachytherapy are:
questions.exp: 'Using Colpostat/Tandem' is the third brachy bullet.

questions.q: Teletherapy's source is printed as:
opts: Outside the body with external beam radiotherapy (EBRT)
questions.exp: The teletherapy column prints outside the body and EBRT.

questions.q: Fill up: The isotope printed for brachytherapy is iridium ____.
questions.exp: The isotope row prints Iridium 192 for brachytherapy.

questions.q: The isotope printed for teletherapy is:
questions.exp: The isotope row prints cesium for teletherapy.

questions.q: Brachytherapy is indicated at what point in the sequence?
questions.exp: The indication row prints 'Following teletherapy' for brachy.

questions.q: Teletherapy is given first to:
questions.exp: 'Given 1st to shrink size of tumour' in the teletherapy column.

questions.q: Point A in brachytherapy is located:
opts: 2 cm above and lateral to external os (parametrial node)
questions.exp: 'Point A : 2 cm above & lateral to external os (Parametrial node)'.

questions.q: Point B is printed as how far from point A, and represents which nodes?
questions.exp: 'Point B : 3 cm away from point A (obturator nodes)'.

questions.q: The teletherapy dose printed is 50 Gy given as:
opts: 5 times a week, 2 Gy per sitting
5 times a week, 3 Gy per sitting
3 times a week, 3 Gy per sitting
questions.exp: The teletherapy other-features cell prints 5 times a week and 2 Gy per sitting.

questions.q: The instrument photographed in the brachytherapy column is captioned:
questions.exp: The photograph caption reads 'Colpostat'.

questions.q: Match each brachytherapy parameter with its printed value - 1) Point A 2) Point B 3) Isotope 4) Sequence ... A) Iridium 192 B) After teletherapy C) 2 cm above and lateral to external os D) 3 cm from point A ... choose:
questions.exp: Point A is 2 cm above and lateral to the external os, point B 3 cm from A, isotope iridium 192 and it follows teletherapy.

questions.q: Odd one out - which statement contradicts the printed table?
opts: Brachytherapy is given first to shrink the tumour
questions.exp: It is teletherapy that is given first to shrink the tumour; brachy follows.

questions.q: True/False: Point A corresponds to the parametrial node region and point B to the obturator nodes.
questions.exp: The brackets print parametrial node for A and obturator nodes for B.

questions.q: Numeric: The teletherapy schedule printed totals 50 Gy; how many Gy per sitting and how many sittings per week?
opts: 1.8 Gy per sitting, 5 times a week
2 Gy per sitting, 3 times a week
2 Gy per sitting, 5 times a week
3 Gy per sitting, 5 times a week
questions.exp: The teletherapy cell prints 5 times a week and 2 Gy per sitting.

questions.q: Numeric: Point A to point B distance and point A to external os distance printed in the brachytherapy diagram are:
questions.exp: The sketch labels 2 cm above the external os to A and 3 cm from A to B.

questions.q: Odd one out - which printed line belongs to teletherapy rather than brachytherapy?
opts: Given 1st to shrink size of tumour
questions.exp: Shrinking the tumour first is the teletherapy indication; the rest are brachytherapy lines.

questions.q: Fill up: Ovarian failure after radiation is printed because the ovary is the most ____ organ.
questions.exp: 'Ovary is most radiosensitive organ'.

questions.q: Fill up: The brachy isotope printed is iridium-192 while teletherapy uses ____.
questions.exp: The isotope row pairs iridium 192 with cesium.

questions.q: The three printed high risk features after surgery are:
opts: Large tumour, LVSI and deep stromal invasion
questions.exp: The high risk column lists margin, parametrium and LN metastasis positive.

questions.q: High risk patients receive which post-operative treatment?
questions.exp: The arrow from high risk ends at post-op chemo radiation.

questions.q: The three printed intermediate risk features are:
opts: Large size of tumour, lymphovascular involvement and deep stromal invasion
questions.exp: The intermediate column lists exactly those three.

questions.q: How many intermediate risk features must be positive to trigger post-op radiotherapy?
questions.exp: The bracket is labelled 'Any 2 +ve'.

questions.q: Intermediate risk patients with any two features receive:
questions.exp: The intermediate arm ends at post-op radiotherapy.

questions.q: Low risk patients receive:
questions.exp: The low risk arm ends at 'No post-op mx'.

questions.q: Match each post-surgery group with its printed treatment - 1) High risk 2) Intermediate risk with any 2 +ve 3) Low risk ... A) No post-op mx B) Post-op chemo radiation C) Post-op radiotherapy ... choose:
questions.exp: High risk gets chemo radiation, intermediate gets radiotherapy and low risk nothing.

questions.q: Scenario: A hysterectomy specimen shows deep stromal invasion and lymphovascular involvement only. The printed post-op plan is:
questions.exp: Two intermediate risk features positive triggers post-op radiotherapy.

questions.q: Odd one out - which feature belongs to the high risk rather than intermediate risk column?
questions.exp: Margin positivity is a high risk feature; the other three are intermediate.

questions.q: True/False: A single intermediate risk feature is enough on the printed page to start post-op radiotherapy.
opts: False - intermediate risk never gets radiotherapy
questions.exp: The bracket requires any 2 positive.

questions.q: Scenario: A post-hysterectomy report shows positive margins with negative parametrium and nodes. The printed adjuvant plan is:
questions.exp: Margin positivity places the case in the high risk column which ends at post-op chemo radiation.
